title: Remote pages and local files in the browser

data.head: Remote pages and local files in the browser — a remote page's favicon and its navigation to a `file:` URL read no local file
data.desc: Remote pages and local files in the browser — a remote page's favicon and its navigation to a file: URL read no local file

body:
The reference browser app (`apps/browser`, the `blitz` binary) closes the two paths by which a remote page still makes
the browser read a local file, which 2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents left open in its report (Insufficient
fixes) because both sit in the app, outside the engine's sub-resource loads:

- **The favicon probe.** A page's favicon candidate — its `<link rel=icon>` href, else `/favicon.ico` joined to its
  base URL — is fetched by `probe_favicon` (`apps/browser/src/favicon.rs`, the fetch at line 50, the entry said 49)
  through `Request::get` with no `initiator`, which `blitz-net` reads as a top-level load and so reads a `file:` URL
  from disk for any document. After this chunk a candidate a non-`file:` document names under `file:` reads no file:
  the probe either carries the loading document as its initiator, so `blitz-net`'s existing `document_may_load` rule
  refuses it `FileForbidden` before any disk read, or is never started. A `file:` document's favicon still loads.

- **Navigation to a `file:` URL.** A link click or form submission on a non-`file:` document navigates through
  `BrowserNavProvider::navigate_to` (`apps/browser/src/history.rs`) → `NavigationOptions::into_request`, whose
  `initiator` is `None`, so the target loads top-level and a `file:` URL is read from disk. After this chunk a
  navigation a non-`file:` document starts to a `file:` URL loads nothing; one a `file:` document starts still loads,
  and the user's own top-level loads (the URL bar, history, home, the new-tab and history pages, the initial URL) are
  unchanged.

- The app only. The engine's sub-resource rule (`document_may_load`, `FileForbidden`) is used as it stands, not
  widened or narrowed; no engine change for every document is planned. [inferred] — P3 confirms the fix reaches no
  engine crate; if it must (e.g. `NavigationOptions` carrying its source document's URL), that is a fork.

- No carrier, verb, argument, cause, session error, exit, log field, span, env read, listener or dependency is added;
  a refused load leaves through the existing error paths and no new log site prints a URL. [inferred]
- The driver, the stand and the seven_guis app are untouched.

- Not in scope: same-origin/CORS, other schemes (`data:`, `about:`), the browser's history store, iframes (already the
  engine's rule).

- **CONTEXT (`cry-s6aydz7c`):** the entry's `CONTEXT: PROVISIONAL` mark. Its placement as a separate chunk is the
  founder's own word, F1 of 2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents answered «A: отдельный чанк (Recommended)»,
  relayed verbatim in `chunks/2026-11-14-auto-exploration/inputs/I6-three-forks-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`. The mark is
  held for the Epoch 4 boundary batch, on the operator's word at the 2026-11-14-auto-exploration wrap, which discharges
  it at this chunk's wrap together with architecture `decision/no-seed-on-carriers` (provisional → standing) and
  `CLAUDE.md`'s seed clause («provisional, the founder's to confirm») — both on the same founder's word (I6, F1 of
  2026-11-14-seeded-randomness). A wrap's batch, not a plan task.

- **CARRY (`cry-no5pm3kz`):** `docs/capabilities.md` still says provisional where the founder has ruled — line 344

  and lines 346–347 («Both are provisional, pending the founder's choice.», exploration on no carrier and following no
  navigation: his A to F1 and F2 at 2026-11-14-auto-exploration,
  `chunks/2026-11-14-auto-exploration/inputs/I6-three-forks-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`,
  `chunks/2026-11-14-auto-exploration/inputs/I9-auto-exploration-f2-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`). Drop both clauses —
  this chunk touches the file (its stated limits gain the browser's two closed paths, if they are stated there).
  Verified at HEAD: line 344 and line 347 (the clause starts on 346) hold the text. [inferred] that the C answer for

- `e73c5ff8c` (the 2026-11-14-auto-exploration wrap commit, the only sha since the last flip): CI#43616972951 —

- **The favicon probe.** A page's favicon candidate — its `<link rel=icon>` href, else `/favicon.ico` joined to its
  base URL — is fetched by `probe_favicon` (`apps/browser/src/favicon.rs`, the fetch at line 50, the entry said 49)
  through `Request::get` with no `initiator`, which `blitz-net` reads as a top-level load and so reads a `file:` URL
  from disk for any document. After this chunk a candidate a non-`file:` document names under `file:` reads no file:
  the probe either carries the loading document as its initiator, so `blitz-net`'s existing `document_may_load` rule
  refuses it `FileForbidden` before any disk read, or is never started. A `file:` document's favicon still loads.
  [premise-corrected: the candidate is chosen synchronously by `favicon_candidate(base_url, href)` (`favicon.rs:20`,
  called once, `document_loader.rs:142`) before any probe or the shared `FAVICON_CACHE` (keyed by candidate, shared
  across tabs) is reached — so the probe is never started: `favicon_candidate` answers none for a candidate
  `document_may_load(Some(base), candidate)` refuses. Gating there also keeps a `file:` icon a `file:` page cached from
  being served to a remote page naming the same URL, which an initiator on the fetch alone would not stop.]

- **Navigation to a `file:` URL.** A link click or form submission on a non-`file:` document navigates through
  `BrowserNavProvider::navigate_to` (`apps/browser/src/history.rs`) → `NavigationOptions::into_request`, whose
  `initiator` is `None`, so the target loads top-level and a `file:` URL is read from disk. After this chunk a
  navigation a non-`file:` document starts to a `file:` URL loads nothing; one a `file:` document starts still loads,
  and the user's own top-level loads (the URL bar, history, home, the new-tab and history pages, the initial URL) are
  unchanged.
  [premise-corrected: `NavigationOptions.source_document` is a document id (`usize`), not a URL
  (`packages/blitz-traits/src/navigation.rs:31`), so the provider cannot read the navigating document's scheme from the
  options; `BrowserNavProvider` is built once per document by `make_doc_config` (`apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs:56`,
  its one construction site), which holds that document's `base_url`. The provider takes that document's URL there and
  refuses, loading nothing, a navigation `document_may_load(document_url, target)` refuses — a document with no URL (the
  error page) counting as no `file:` document. This adds `apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs` to the files the change
  reaches. Reading the tab's current history entry instead would let a remote page still displayed while a `file:` page
  the user typed loads navigate to a `file:` URL. Silent refusal, as Chromium («Not allowed to load local resource») and
  Firefox do; the Fetch standard leaves `file:` to the implementation (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-fetch).
  Every link-click, keyboard-activated link or submit, and form-submission navigation of the top document reaches
  `navigate_to` (`packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:1140`, `packages/blitz-dom/src/form.rs:168`); an iframe's
  navigation goes through the engine's own `IframeNavigationProvider` and `stamped_request`, already the engine's rule.]

- The app only. The engine's sub-resource rule (`document_may_load`, `FileForbidden`) is used as it stands, not
  widened or narrowed; no engine change for every document is planned. Verified at P3: both fixes sit in
  `apps/browser` (a leaf crate — no inbound crate edge, code-graph `crate_edges`), reading the public
  `blitz_traits::net::document_may_load` as it stands; no engine crate is edited.

- **CARRY (`cry-no5pm3kz`):** `docs/capabilities.md` still says provisional where the founder has ruled — line 344

  `chunks/2026-11-14-auto-exploration/inputs/I6-three-forks-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`,
  `chunks/2026-11-14-auto-exploration/inputs/I9-auto-exploration-f2-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`). Drop both clauses —
  this chunk touches the file for it. Verified at HEAD: line 344 and line 347 (the clause starts on 346) hold the text;
  the C answer is snapped as `chunks/2026-11-14-start-in-a-state/inputs/I4-start-in-a-state-f1-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`

  is upstream's (no escher contract row covers its favicon or navigation path), and its «Loading pages» limit speaks of

- Every new check the plan names carries a control (test-plan `decision/mutation-controlled-tests`): the mutation or

  named none. [premise-corrected: no `StdNetProvider`, temp file or `TMPDIR` read is needed — the favicon gate is the
  pure `favicon_candidate`, unit-tested in `favicon.rs`'s existing test module; the navigation gate is reached by

- `packages/blitz-traits/src/net.rs` (55–110) — `Request.initiator` (65); `document_may_load(document_url: Option<&Url>, url: &Url) -> bool` (95): `url.scheme() != "file" || document_url.is_some_and(|d| d.scheme() == "file")`.

- `packages/blitz-traits/src/navigation.rs` (1–80) — `NavigationOptions { url, content_type, source_document: usize, method, document_resource }` (`#[non_exhaustive]`, pub fields, `NavigationOptions::new(url, content_type, source_document)`); `into_request` sets `initiator: None`.

- `packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs` (150–175, 255–285) — `fetch_inner`'s `file` arm refuses `FileForbidden` only when an initiator is present and `document_may_load` refuses; `fetch_async` carries the request into it unchanged.

- `packages/blitz-dom/src/iframe.rs` (1–80) — an iframe's navigations go through `IframeNavigationProvider` → `DocumentEvent::NavigateIframe`, reloaded through `stamped_request` (the engine's rule), never through the browser's provider.

- **probe_favicon / probe_favicon_cached** — `probe_favicon_cached` @ `favicon.rs:36`; `commit_loaded_document` @ `apps/browser/src/tab.rs:160`. Untouched.
- **make_doc_config** — 2 callers, both in `DocumentLoader::load_document` @ `document_loader.rs:122` and `:155`. Signature unchanged (it already holds `base_url`).

- **BrowserNavProvider** — refs: its definition `history.rs:104`, `use` @ `document_loader.rs:13`, its one construction @ `document_loader.rs:55`; `git grep -n BrowserNavProvider` over tracked files gives the same three code sites.
- **crate_edges** — `browser` has no inbound edge (a leaf crate); outbound to blitz-traits, blitz-net, blitz-dom, dioxus-native, … — the change has no cross-crate blast radius.

- **A `file:` rule by loading document** (`packages/blitz-traits/src/net.rs:95`): `document_may_load` is the one predicate every refusal of the rule calls (script fetcher, blitz-net's `file` arm); a document with no URL counts as no `file:` document.

- **An in-memory tab history in a unit test** (`apps/browser/src/tab.rs:301-342`): a component builds `Store::new_maybe_sync(History::new(Request::get(…)))`, and `VirtualDom::new(app).rebuild_in_place()` runs it, the assertions inside the component.

- **Inline test modules at file end** (`apps/browser/src/favicon.rs:72`, `tab.rs:296`): `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with `use super::*`; the browser's test modules allow `clippy::expect_used` with no justification (arch `decision/justified-expect-unwrap`'s stated except), `unwrap()` used on fixture URL parses in `tab.rs`.

- **Spec citation at the implementation** (arch `decision/spec-url-citations`, `decision/cite-the-spec`): cite https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-fetch beside each gate and name the browsers whose behaviour it follows (Chromium refuses a remote page's `file:` load, «Not allowed to load local resource»).

- **std Result under the Dioxus prelude glob** (arch `decision/std-result-under-dioxus-prelude`): `history.rs` globs `dioxus_native::prelude::*` at line 3 — any two-parameter result there is spelled `std::result::Result`.
- **Fixture precondition first** (arch `decision/fixture-precondition-first`): each test asserts its fixture's scheme before the behaviour.
- **Silent checks** (obs `decision/checks-silent`): no subscriber, env read or print in a test.
- **Unresolvable URL skipped, never a panic** (arch `decision/unresolvable-url-skipped`): `Url::parse` of the base stays fallible (`.ok()`), no `unwrap` in shipped code.

- `apps/browser/src/history.rs` — `BrowserNavProvider` holds its document's URL and `navigate_to` loads nothing for a target `document_may_load` refuses; a new test module at the file's end
- `apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs` — `make_doc_config` hands `BrowserNavProvider` the document's own URL, parsed from `base_url`

data.head: # Plan — 2026-11-14-remote-pages-local-files: "Remote pages and local files in the browser"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-14-remote-pages-local-files · **Version:** escher-0.3.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-14T17:20:51Z

The reference browser app (`apps/browser`, the `blitz` binary) stops a remote page from making it read a local file
by the two paths 2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents left open: the favicon probe and a navigation the page
starts. Both are gated in the app by the engine's own predicate, `blitz_traits::net::document_may_load`, used as it
stands (arch · decision/file-url-load-rule; security-plan · decision/file-urls-only-from-file-documents): a favicon
candidate a non-`file:` document names under `file:` is never chosen, so neither the probe nor the shared favicon
cache is reached; and a navigation a non-`file:` document starts to a `file:` URL loads nothing, silently, as
Chromium and Firefox refuse it (arch · decision/cite-the-spec). A `file:` document keeps its `file:` favicon and its
`file:` links, and the user's own loads (URL bar, history, home, the about pages, the first tab) are untouched.

No engine crate changes, no request carries a new initiator, and nothing reaches blitz-net's `FileForbidden` path: a
refused favicon or navigation is simply not started, so no log site, span, field, env read, dependency or carrier is
added (obs · decision/checks-silent; security-plan · contract/blitz-net-provider-error/file-forbidden unchanged). It is
a narrowing of an existing input surface in an upstream-only app, not a boundary widening — the precedent that classed
`document_may_load` itself (security history n=4).

The chunk also folds its CARRY: `docs/capabilities.md` drops the two «provisional» clauses the founder has since ruled
on (his C, `chunks/2026-11-14-start-in-a-state/inputs/I4-start-in-a-state-f1-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`; his A to F1
and F2, `chunks/2026-11-14-auto-exploration/inputs/I6-three-forks-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`,
`chunks/2026-11-14-auto-exploration/inputs/I9-auto-exploration-f2-founder-2026-11-14.md.txt`). Every new check names
its control (test-plan · decision/mutation-controlled-tests; the operator's directive, inputs#I1).

1. **Favicon gate** — `apps/browser/src/favicon.rs`, `favicon_candidate(base_url, favicon_href)`: after the candidate
   is resolved (the href joined to the parsed base, else `/favicon.ico`), keep it only where
   `document_may_load(Some(&base), &candidate)` allows it; otherwise answer `None`. Import `document_may_load` from
   `blitz_traits::net` beside `Url`. Cite https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-fetch above the filter and say in one
   `///` line on the function that a non-`file:` page names no `file:` favicon (Chromium's «Not allowed to load local
   resource»). The function's signature, its one caller (`document_loader.rs:142`), `probe_favicon`, the cache and
   which href is read (design-system · decision/favicon-from-first-icon-link) stay as they are. Keeps arch S4.

2. **Favicon checks** — append three tests to `favicon.rs`'s existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (line 72), each
   asserting its fixture's scheme first (arch S2): `remote_page_favicon_candidate_names_no_local_file`
   (base `https://example.com/page.html`, href `file:///etc/hosts` → `None`);
   `file_page_favicon_candidate_keeps_local_file` (base `file:///tmp/page.html`, href `icon.png` → `Some` of
   `file:///tmp/icon.png`); `remote_page_default_favicon_candidate_unchanged` (base `https://example.com/page.html`, no
   href → `Some` of `https://example.com/favicon.ico`). Fixture URLs are literals in the test (tests S4); no disk read,
   no temp dir, no `TMPDIR`, no print (obs S1). Keeps tests S2, S3, S4, S5; arch S1, S2, S3.

3. **Navigation gate** — `apps/browser/src/history.rs`: `BrowserNavProvider` gains a private
   `document_url: Option<Url>` field and a constructor `BrowserNavProvider::for_document(history, base_url:
   Option<&str>)` that parses the base (`Url::parse(..).ok()` — an unparsable or absent base reads as no URL, never a
   panic: arch · decision/unresolvable-url-skipped). `navigate_to` returns at once, loading nothing, when
   `document_may_load(self.document_url.as_ref(), &options.url)` refuses; otherwise it pushes as today. No `tracing`
   call on the refusal. Cite the Fetch standard URL and Chromium's behaviour above the check; `///` on the new field and
   constructor. The file globs `dioxus_native::prelude::*` (line 3): a two-parameter result added here is spelled
   `std::result::Result` (arch S5). Keeps arch S4, S5.

4. **Wire the document's URL** — `apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs`, `make_doc_config`: build the provider as
   `BrowserNavProvider::for_document(history, base_url.as_deref())` in place of the struct literal at line 56; nothing
   else in the config moves (`..Default::default()` keeps the default UA sheet: design-system ·
   decision/default-ua-sheet-via-default-config). The error page's config (`base_url` `None`) thereby reads as no
   `file:` document.

5. **Navigation checks** — a new `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the end of `history.rs` (arch S1; tests S2), modelled on
   `tab.rs`'s `tab_lens_survives_webview_props_replacement` (a `History` store built with `Store::new_maybe_sync`
   inside a component run by `VirtualDom::new(app).rebuild_in_place()`, assertions inside the component). Three tests,
   each asserting first the scheme of its document and of its target (arch S2), then calling
   `navigate_to(NavigationOptions::new(target, None, 0))` on a provider from `for_document` and reading the store's
   current URL: `remote_page_navigation_to_file_url_loads_nothing` (document `https://example.com/`, target
   `file:///etc/hosts` → current URL still the initial one); `file_page_navigation_to_file_url_loads` (document
   `file:///tmp/page.html`, target `file:///tmp/other.html` → current URL the target);
   `remote_page_navigation_to_https_url_loads` (document `https://example.com/`, target `https://example.org/` →
   current URL the target). No print, env read or disk read. Keeps tests S2–S6; arch S1–S3; obs S1; security S1, S2.

6. **The CARRY** — `docs/capabilities.md`: delete the sentence «This is provisional, pending the founder's choice.»
   (line 344) and «Both are provisional, pending the founder's choice.» (lines 346–347), re-flowing the two bullets'
   lines to the file's width; nothing else in the file changes (its pinned names and counts, its other sections — a11y
   history n=5 — and the «Escher» spelling stand).

7. **Controls** — implement fires one `gate.py control` (gate-contract.md §Control) against the browser unit entry
   (entry 1 below), the controls file naming per control the edit and its case (each case the test's name alone):
   - C1 `favicon-gate-removed`: drop the `document_may_load` filter in `favicon_candidate` → case
     `remote_page_favicon_candidate_names_no_local_file` reads failed.
   - C2 `favicon-gate-refuses-all`: make the filter refuse every candidate → cases
     `file_page_favicon_candidate_keeps_local_file` and `remote_page_default_favicon_candidate_unchanged` read failed.
   - C3 `nav-gate-removed`: drop the early return in `navigate_to` → case
     `remote_page_navigation_to_file_url_loads_nothing` reads failed.
   - C4 `nav-url-dropped`: have `for_document` store no URL (`document_url: None`) → case
     `file_page_navigation_to_file_url_loads` reads failed (this controls the base's parse too).
   - C5 `nav-gate-refuses-all`: make `navigate_to` return for every target → case
     `remote_page_navigation_to_https_url_loads` reads failed.
   Every control must read `holds`; the summary line and each control's line go to the chunk's evidence. The CARRY's
   probe (entry 3) is controlled by its own baseline: it reads red on the untouched tree (2 hits) and green after
   step 6.
8. **Pre-push gate** — run entry 4 (`fast`) last among the local entries; a red stops the operator pass's push.

- `apps/browser/src/favicon.rs` — `favicon_candidate` filtered by `document_may_load`; three tests in its test module
- `apps/browser/src/history.rs` — `BrowserNavProvider.document_url`, `for_document`, the early return in `navigate_to`; a new test module
- `apps/browser/src/document_loader.rs` — `make_doc_config` builds the provider through `for_document`
- `docs/capabilities.md` — the two «provisional» clauses dropped

`test {path} ... ok` line), the CARRY's probe, the doc leg is not listed (no library crate changes: the browser is a
binary, not documented — arch S6's rustdoc gate unaffected), and the local pre-push gate `fast` (fmt → clippy →
workspace tests → CI scripts, where `test_capability_statement.py` re-reads `docs/capabilities.md` → embolden). No
live leg and no smoke entry: nothing launches the app or mints an id (test-plan · absence/windowed-end-to-end-tests).
The diff adds no OS-conditional site, but the plan claims the new tests read alike on linux, windows and macOS, so it
carries the operator's hygiene, push and CI entries; the CI entry's note names the legs.
